text: This is Tiny.
Tiny is a very small AI. And Tiny is... terrible at maths.
Let me try! Ask it three plus four, and... eight! Six?! Twelve!
Four times out of five, it’s wrong.
Now watch.
Sixty rounds later, Tiny gets it right nine times out of ten!
And here’s the strange part.
Nobody ever told Tiny the answer. Not once.
Wait. Nobody told it? Then how on earth did it learn?
That’s exactly what this video is about. And it’s the same trick that taught DeepSeek R1 to reason.
The nudge. Episode one.
You already know this trick. You’ve probably used it on a dog.
Oh, like teaching a puppy to sit? You can’t exactly explain the word sit to a puppy.
Exactly. So you wait. And the moment it happens to sit...
Treat!
It has no idea why. But next time, it sits a little sooner.
Rewarded things happen more often. That’s the whole trick. Now, let’s do it to Tiny.
Here’s what’s going on inside Tiny’s head.
For three plus four, Tiny isn’t sure. Every answer has a chance.
Six gets about a third. Eight, thirty percent.
Hang on. And seven, the right answer? Only about one in five?
Yep. When Tiny answers, it’s like rolling a loaded die. Mostly its favourites. Sometimes not.
Ooh, let’s roll it a few times.
Six. Eight. Seven! Six. Twelve.
Same question, different answers. Remember that. It’s going to matter.
Now, Tiny says seven. Our grader checks it, and gives Tiny a treat: a reward of one.
So what happens to the chance of seven?
Pause, and have a guess.
I’m going with A! It got a treat, so now it knows the answer is seven. Right?
Close, but no. It’s B. It goes up a little. Not to a hundred percent. Just a nudge.
One treat doesn’t make Tiny certain. It just makes seven a bit more likely next time.
Here’s the nudge.
Seven earned a treat, so seven becomes a little more likely.
After one step, it goes from twenty-two percent to forty-six!
And the others shrink to make room?
Right. Six, eight and twelve all shrink. The chances always add up to a hundred.
Stop and think about that for a second.
Nobody told Tiny that the answer is seven.
And nobody explained addition!
Tiny only heard one thing: that was good.
Now do that again. And again.
Ask, roll, grade, nudge. Sixty rounds.
Every time Tiny gets it right, seven creeps up. And notice these flat stretches.
Hmm. What are those flat bits?
Hold on to that question. Twenty rounds in, seven is at about forty percent. Sixty rounds in, Tiny is right nine times out of ten!
No single step did much. Together, they changed Tiny’s mind. That, really, is what training is.
Quick recap.
Tiny doesn’t have one answer. It has chances.
A treat makes the answer it gave a bit more likely.
And lots of small nudges add up to real learning.
But there’s a problem. Remember those flat stretches?
Watch what happens when Tiny gets it wrong.
Tiny says eight. Wrong. Reward: zero.
And the nudge is zero, times anything. Nothing moves.
Wait. So a mistake teaches Tiny absolutely nothing? But that’s most of its answers!
Exactly. In the next episode, we fix that, with one simple idea you already know from school.
Try nudging Tiny’s chances yourself, in the tool below this video.
See you in the next episode!
